review_basis: Local engineering inspection of the complete admitted public PDFs, selected physical-page text and rendered pages; no field or independent-domain claim.
candidate_policy: Provider statements are unreviewed candidates. Accepted documentary facts are not operational inventory, demand, locations, or water stocks without separate readiness review.

items.source_fact: The plan estimates a city population of 2.86 million in a section citing the 2010 census; this is historical city context, not selected-area evacuation demand.
Talayan, Damayang Lagi, Roxas, St. Peter and Dona Imelda are listed as the top flood-impact priority barangays. This ranking does not define pickup demand or road closures.
One permanent evacuation area per each of six districts is a 2021-2027 project output, not six verified current shelters or capacities.
Portable drinking-water stations are mentioned with a purchase activity; no usable initial shelter water volume is stated.
Water purification tablets and safe-drinking-water objectives are listed; initial per-shelter potable stock and delivery rate remain unknown.
Page 111 lists Annexes A-D, while the supplied volume ends with a blank page 112; the substantive annex contents are not present in this source.

review_warnings: A provider value of 100% with COUNT unit was rejected during replay; percentages cannot be counted as facilities.
No city-wide quantity is promoted to the selected study-area population or shelter inventory.

items.source_fact: The 2020 census population is 112,889 across 14 barangays. It is not the same as flood exposure or scenario evacuation demand.
In June 2014, 11,861 of 20,194 households were reported with Level 3 water connections; the plan separately mentions 23 pumping stations. Neither is a measured initial shelter water stock.
The flood section lists 56,516 affected people and 11,300 affected households. These overlap the municipality population and are not added to it.
The visually inspected table prints 11.43 square kilometres under high flood susceptibility and 10.01 under low-to-moderate susceptibility; these are areas, not people or evacuation demand.
The split table labels school, day-care and covered-court capacities in FAMILY units. Day-care entries use the 5-6 range; no family-to-person factor is supplied by this table.
Printed capacity subtotals 2,753 + 84 + 400 + 500 + 50 + 200 sum to 3,987 FAMILY, while the printed grand total is 4,087 FAMILY. Both values are retained as a critical conflict.

Page 121 uses graphic checks/crosses for facility presence and prints GMACC, Kanlungan and Municipal Hall capacities in shared columns. Provider assignments of those shared capacities to Cutcut are rejected pending location/capacity review; blank cells are unknown, not zero.
Barangay halls are stated pickup points, with barangay/municipal service vehicles and walking or small/medium vehicle access described. Seats, exact schedules and road times are not established.

The table is headed Proposed/Programs/Projects/Activities and includes rescue vehicle/boat procurement costs. The provider mislabeled currency values as COUNT; those candidates are rejected and cannot become fleet inventory.
The plan calls GMACC the primary evacuation center. Its exact coordinate, access connector and reconciled capacity are not supplied by that sentence.

review_warnings: The 2023-2025 plan period is historical for a later scenario; applicability must be acknowledged.
A 7.6 water-use candidate on page 126 has a per-person dimension requiring source and model-unit review before promotion.
Provider slice-relative citations on the split table were normalized only where region ID and group page position agreed; the raw response remains unchanged.
